description: Connection rules for the clue graph: which node kinds may fill which premise role of an inference, and which kinds a relation may join. A first proposal, meant to become the game's edge-type rules (a clue's type decides what it can connect to). Enforced by scripts/validate_case.py.

physical.card: An object or body: something you can pick up or look at.

trace.card: A mark left behind: tracks, prints, mud, stains.

document.card: Something written: a bill, a betting book, a lab report.

testimony.card: What someone says. Carries a speaker and a reliability.

observation.card: What the investigator notices first-hand: weather, a reaction, a state of affairs.

absence.card: Something that did NOT happen or is NOT there. The dog that did nothing.

background.card: General knowledge about how the world works. Never about this case; used as a rule.

inference.card: A conclusion drawn from other nodes. Exists only as the conclusion of an inference.

hypothesis.card: A theory someone holds. May be false. Can be supported, refuted, or tested.

fact.card: Something taken as true about the case.

rule.card: A general truth the step applies.

assumption.card: A theory adopted for the sake of the step (a working hypothesis).

pattern_hints.elimination: Usually has an absence premise, or concludes 'not X' / 'therefore the remaining option'.
pattern_hints.identification: Needs at least two fact premises that describe the same thing from different sides.
pattern_hints.prediction_confirmed: Has an assumption (the hypothesis) plus the fact that was found because it was looked for.
pattern_hints.abduction: The conclusion explains its premises; strength is rarely 'certain'.
